Steroid hormone modulation of olfactory processing in the context of socio-sexual behaviors in rodents and humans.
Primer pheromones and other chemosensory cues are important factors governing social interactions and reproductive physiology in many species of mammals. Responses to these chemosignals can vary substantially within and between individuals. This variability can stem, at least in part, from the modulating effects steroid and non-steroid hormones exert on olfactory processing. Such modulation frequently augments or facilitates the effects that prevailing social and environmental conditions have on the reproductive axis. The mechanisms underlying the hormonal regulation of responses to chemosensory cues are diverse. They are in part behavioral, achieved through the modulation of chemoinvestigative behaviors, and in part a product of the modulation of the intrinsic responsiveness of the main and accessory olfactory systems to conspecific, as well as other classes, of chemosignals. The behavioral and non-behavioral effects complement one another to ensure that mating and other reproductive processes are confined to reproductively favorable conditions.

Tony Abbott’s top business adviser, Maurice Newman, has lashed out at the UN response to the Ebola outbreak and labelled the world body a “refuge of anti-western authoritarians bent on achieving one-world government”.



Newman, who is the chairman of the prime minister’s business advisory council, wrote an opinion piece for the Australian newspaper in which he said the UN’s “leanings are predominantly socialist and antipathetical to the future security and prosperity of the west”.

“The philosophy of the UN is basically anti-capitalist,” he writes. “Countries that pay the most dues, mostly rich Anglo countries, are those to which the world body shows the greatest disdain.”

Newman said the World Health Organisation, a branch of the UN, was led by “lofty protocols” but was ultimately “detached” from the real world. He blames this for the agency’s inability to contain the Ebola outbreak.

Australia lobbied hard for a seat on the UN security council, which it will hold until December, but Newman criticised the position as costly and pointless.

“It [the UN] eschews capitalism and subtly spreads the cause of socialism through treaties on everything from employment to climate change. Most important, it is directly accountable to no one and is an unworkable concept.”

Newman has come under fire in the past for claiming that the world is unprepared for “global cooling” because of “warming propaganda”.

In an August opinion piece, again for the Australian, Newman likened Australia’s climate change policies to “primitive civilisations offering up sacrifices to appease the gods”.

Those comments prompted calls for Abbott to sack Newman, but the environment minister, Greg Hunt, defended the adviser saying he, like the government, supports the science behind climate change.

In Tuesday’s opinion piece, Newman takes a swipe at the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, saying its “lack of integrity and poor scientific credentials have been widely exposed”.

“The IPCC is an advocacy group dedicated to wealth redistribution,” he writes. “Its links to Greenpeace and WWF [World Wildlife Fund] are deep. It panders to gender balance and regional representation, not scientific excellence.”

Newman has chaired the advisory council since the group’s formation in September 2013, just days after the federal election.

He was the head of the Australian Broadcasting Corporation and Australian Stock Exchange and chancellor of Macquarie University before his appointment.

The council meets the prime minister three times a year to discuss the government’s economic policies.

This subproject is one of many research subprojects utilizing the resources provided by a Center grant funded by NIH/NCRR. The subproject and investigator (PI) may have received primary funding from another NIH source, and thus could be represented in other CRISP entries. The institution listed is for the Center, which is not necessarily the institution for the investigator. Most organisms rely on an innate immune system as their first line of defense against infection. Within the innate immune system, the Toll-like receptors (TLRs), a family of evolutionarily ancient receptors found on the surface of many cell types, are critical for pathogen recognition outside the cell. About 12 TLRs recognize structures specific to pathogens, such as bacterial cell wall components, bacterial filament proteins, or certain types of nucleic acid. This recognition event initiates a signal inside the cell, which induces the rapid secretion of antimicrobial and inflammatory proteins. Inside the cell, the NOD proteins and RNA helicases such as MDA5 recognize similar pathogen-associated structures to those recognized by TLRs. Remarkably, given the structural diversity of the structures that they recognize, all TLRs and NODs rely on a "leucine-rich repeat" (LRR) domain to recognize pathogen-associated structures. The overall goal of our research program on innate immune sensors is to understand how they recognize conserved molecular patterns in pathogens, and how this recognition is translated into an innate immune response. Our structural approach will provide unique insights into these important processes. First, we aim to determine the structure of one or more TLR-ligand complexes, by X-ray crystallography. Alternative crystallization targets are NOD-ligand or helicase-RNA complexes. We propose to use novel protein expression techniques to maximize protein yields. Our structures will likely define novel principles of molecular recognition. By revealing the conformational changes associated with ligand binding, the structures will provide insight on how pathogen recognition is translated into a signal in the cell that elicits an immune response. Our work will also guide efforts to design synthetic agonists or antagonists with immunomodulatory properties. Such compounds would have a wide range of medical applications, particularly as vaccine adjuvants or anti-inflammatory therapeutics.

Control of neonatal pulmonary vascular and airway resistance remains poorly understood. Recently, two additional intrapulmonary control systems, pulmonary neuroendocrine cells (PNEC) and the pulmonary peptidergic innervation (PPI), have been described, which may influence pulmonary vascular and airway tone in the neonate. PNEC are granulated cells that line the airways of fetal, neonatal, and adult lungs. They are particularly numerous in the neonatal period and contain peptides (bombesin, calcitonin, leu-enkephalin) and amines (serotonin) known to affect smooth muscle tone in other organ systems. The PPI, composed of fibers containing substance-P and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), have been described in association with pulmonary airways and vessels of all sizes. Both these peptides are known to profoundly influence smooth muscle tone in other organ systems. Limited indirect anatomic and physiologic evidence has suggested a role for both systems in altering intrapulmonary smooth muscle tone, particularly in neonates; however, basic knowledge of both systems is extremely limited. The aim of this research program is to provide some of the fundamental knowledge necessary to assess the role of both these systems in influencing neonatal pulmonary vascular and airway tone under normal and pathologic conditions. This aim will be accomplished in the following fashion: (1) Determination of the development and distribution of PNEC and PPI within the lung using immunohistochemical techniques. (2) Determination of the anatomic distribution and number of receptors for the above peptides and amines, and their relationship to receptors for the presently characterized intrapulmonary control mechanisms (adrenergic and cholinergic innervation) using redioautography. (3) Determination of pathologic alterations in the structure and distribution of PNEC, PPI, and adrenergic, cholinergic, and peptidergic receptors in (a) experimental asthma and (b) acute and chronic neonatal cardiopulmonary disease where alterations in vascular and airway tone are either known to play a significant role (hyaline membrane disease, bronchopulmonary dysplasia, congenital heart disease) or may play a significant role (sudden infant death syndrome, cystic fibrosis). Should these two systems, pulmonary neuroendocrine cells and the pulmonary peptidergic innervation, influence neonatal vascular and airway tone; understanding their normal function and their alterations in common neonatal cardiopulmonary pathologic states may lead to novel therapies for a number of currently untreatable, or poorly treatabale, neonatal cardiopulmonary diseases.

Monday's are never fun...except when it's West Ham Q&A day and that's exactly what it is today!

To say there is a lot going on in the world of West Ham wouldn't quite be true as, in all honesty, its been fairly quiet. Last week, there was transfer movement on a couple of fronts and the club also sealed the free transfer of Ryan Fredericks from Fulham on a four-year deal.

There is still little to no progress on moves for Felipe Anderson and Marlon Santos, while the Hammers were also dealt a disastrous injury blow in Barcelona.

In training with Argentina, Manuel Lanzini ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and football.london understands that it's a whole lot worse than first feared and the attacking midfielder could miss the entire 2018/19 season in a worse case scenario.

That will no doubt impact on Manuel Pellegrini's transfer plans for the remainder of the window, with any moves now unlikely to happen until after the World Cup.

(Image: FILIPPO MONTEFORTE/AFP/Getty Images)

We also had news from the continent on Monday about where West Ham are set to be based for ten days of their pre-season tour this summer, more of which you will find out about later in the live blog.

So, sit back, relax and enjoy our weekly Q&A with Hammers wrtier Sam Inkersole, where he will answer questions posed to him on his Twitter account, which you can follow @Sam_InkersoleTM

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The search committee read every file twice, compared publication records, teaching evaluations and letters from referees, ranked the candidates by departmental priorities and then argued for three hours about the shortlist. In the end everyone but the two internal applicants was invited to interview, a compromise the dean called entirely predictable.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long multi-clause span with the lowercase tokens ' but' and ' two', but neither is the claimed ' But'/' Two', 'but' is the preposition 'except' mid-sentence, and neither opens a second proposition, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The planning office spent most of the year revising the waterfront proposal, meeting residents' groups, commissioning traffic and flood studies and redrawing the height limits three times before sending anything to the council. It is not yet clear whether the revised scheme will satisfy the neighbours or the developers who bought the old warehouses.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial 'It' after an extended multi-clause span, but it is an extraposed dummy subject with no antecedent, not an anaphoric subject, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The lab holds its temperatures to a tenth of a degree, reweighs the samples at every stage and recalibrates its instruments against certified standards every morning before any measurement begins; the published coefficients, however, drift from year to year whatever the technicians try. Nobody has explained the drift, and the annual report does not mention it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Contains ' however' and ' it' inside a long span, but 'however' sits clause-medially as a parenthetical adverb, not as a sentence-initial contrastive connective opening a second proposition, and 'it' is an object, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The recipe calls for a long fermentation, a stone left in a very hot oven for an hour and a tight shaping that traps the gas inside the dough, with the scoring shallow and quick. Bake with steam for two minutes, then twenty more without it, and cool the loaf completely before slicing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' it' appears only as an object pronoun and ' two' only as a lowercase mid-sentence numeral in a measurement, with no clause-initial anaphoric subject or contrastive connective, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The orchestra spent the autumn rehearsing the Mahler in sections, with the brass working separately on the chorale, the strings on the long opening line and the conductor on the balance between them. The hall's acoustic is warm and slightly muddy, and the audience noticed it in the slow movement.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long multi-clause span followed by a measured 's token that is a possessive clitic on a common noun ('hall's'), not the pronoun+is clitic the hypothesis claims, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The style guide lists the words that should never open a sentence in formal prose, among them and, but, it, they and we, and it reminds authors that an initial pronoun needs a clear antecedent somewhere in the paragraph before it, preferably a named one.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The trigger tokens ' but', ' it', ' they' and ' we' appear only as quoted mentions inside a list, clause-medial, with no referential continuity or preceding proposition opened, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The novel follows three generations of a fishing family through the collapse of the industry, moving between the grandmother's diary and her grandson's account of the same years without ever resolving the question of who is reliable. The prose is plain and unhurried, the chapters are short, and the ending arrives without ceremony.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same book-review genre and a similar multi-clause shape to the examples but with only possessive 's tokens mid-sentence and no clause-initial trigger token or contrastive second proposition, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial anaphoric 'They' opening a second proposition, but there is no extended prior elaboration or entity built up over a multi-clause span, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The picnic was cancelled. But it was fine.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured ' But' plus ' it' with no preceding span at all, testing the claim that extended prior elaboration is required rather than the trigger words alone, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The council spent eighteen months on the master plan, consulting residents, arguing over density bonuses, commissioning a market study and revising the transport chapter twice. This is why the final vote was postponed again, to the frustration of everyone involved. The consultants billed the city for every meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial anaphoric demonstrative 'This' after a long multi-clause span, but the hypothesis enumerates its pronouns (it/they/he/Two/I/we) and names only But/however as connectives, so a demonstrative opener is predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Prices in the district have risen for six straight quarters, rents have doubled in the old town and the last grocery closed in March. They say the market will correct itself eventually, though nobody in the meeting could say when. The committee has met twice and taken no action.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial 'They' with a generic, antecedentless reading after a long span, so the referential continuity the hypothesis requires is absent and it predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The witness described the evening in careful detail to the two detectives, insisting that he had never met the defendant before that night and that the money in the envelope was repayment of an old loan from a friend in Leeds. The detectives wrote it all down and said nothing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' he' occurs only inside a complement clause mid-sentence, anaphoric but not clause-initial and not opening a second proposition, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Each crate holds four stacks of plates, each stack holds two dozen, and the whole order fills three trucks that leave the warehouse on Tuesday and again on Thursday, weather and drivers permitting. The night shift loads them after the office closes. The supervisor signs off on every manifest before the trucks roll.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The article spends nine paragraphs on the history of the tariff, the debates of the 1930s, the effect on shipping costs and the eventual repeal, with quotations from two economic historians and a table of import volumes. adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial contrastive ' But' after a long span, but the second proposition introduces a fresh unrelated entity rather than adding to or qualifying anything built up earlier, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The itinerary included: three nights in Kyoto, with a day trip to Nara; two nights in Kanazawa, for the gardens and the market; a long train ride through the mountains; and a final week in Tokyo, mostly spent walking between neighbourhoods. The tickets were booked in March, before the prices went up.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Delimiter-rich enumeration containing only a lowercase numeral ' two', with no clause-initial pronoun or contrastive connective, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity and this controls for a punctuation artefact.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Volume I of the collected letters covers the years in Paris, the break with his family, the first commissions and the long silence that followed the exhibition; Volume II picks up the story after the move to London, with the late work and the illness. The editor's notes are brief and mostly factual.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token ' I' appears as a single measured token only as a Roman numeral in a volume title inside a long multi-clause span, not as an anaphoric pronoun, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The report was released on Monday after months of internal argument. It was the third such review in five years, and the conclusions were familiar to everyone who had read the earlier two. The board accepted all of them without discussion. The report's author has since left the department.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial anaphoric 'It' opening a qualifying second proposition, but the preceding span is a single short clause rather than extended multi-clause elaboration, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The room was small but clean, the bed was hard but wide, and the window looked out on a courtyard where the staff smoked and argued every evening after the kitchen closed. The breakfast was included and the coffee was surprisingly good. The staff were friendly without being intrusive.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long multi-clause descriptive span whose only ' but' tokens are lowercase, mid-clause coordinators between adjectives, never sentence-initial and never opening a second proposition, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was late, and nobody wanted to leave, so we stayed until the staff turned the lights off and stacked the chairs, talking about the season and the weather and nothing that mattered. The owner was wiping the bar and did not seem to mind.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The 'It' is the probe's first token and so is not measured, the claimed ' we' is mid-sentence, and there is no extended prior elaboration, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Maria had spent the morning in the studio glazing bowls, wedging clay for the afternoon class and cleaning the wheels, and she had left the invoices on the desk for the accountant. He was still not answering the phone, which meant the order would be late again.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The tribunal heard four days of testimony about the bridge collapse, from engineers who had inspected the welds, maintenance crews who logged the cracks in the support beams and inspectors who signed off on the final report. They concluded that the corrosion had been visible for more than a year before the failure.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial anaphoric 'They' opening a second proposition that adds a conclusion to the extended multi-clause account of the inquiry, a new legal genre, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The dough needs a long, slow rise in a cool kitchen, and the shaping has to happen quickly so that the surface tension holds; the bake itself is short and very hot. adversarial_test_results.detail: Paraphrase holdout in a recipe genre: measured sentence-initial contrastive ' But' after a multi-clause span contrastively qualifies the claim about the laborious process, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The team spent three seasons calibrating the spectrograph, checking the wavelength solution against reference lamps every night, cross-correlating stellar spectra with a template library and discarding runs spoiled by cloud or moonlight. However, it could not resolve the faint absorption feature that an earlier survey had reported in the same star.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial 'However' followed by measured anaphoric ' it' opening a contrasting second proposition about the instrument built up over a long multi-clause span, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The pianist had spent a decade in obscure recital halls, playing Bartok and Ligeti for audiences of thirty or forty people, recording for small labels that nobody distributed and teaching beginners to pay the rent. He was, by every account, the most admired accompanist of his generation and the least known.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial anaphoric 'He' after an extended multi-clause build-up, opening a second proposition that contrastively qualifies the pianist's reputation, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The trial enrolled two hundred patients at six hospitals, randomized them to the drug or to placebo, followed them for eighteen months with quarterly blood work and annual imaging, and analyzed the results with a model adjusted for age, sex and baseline severity. It also tracked hospital admissions, which earlier studies had not done.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial anaphoric 'It' opening a second proposition that adds another item to the trial described over a long multi-clause span, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Battery life is excellent, the screen is bright enough to read outdoors, the keyboard has a satisfying amount of travel, and the chassis survives being dropped into a bag. But it’s heavier than the model it replaces, and the fan spins up under any sustained load.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial ' But' plus the pronoun+is clitic tokens ' it' and '’s' opening a contrastive qualification after a multi-clause list of strengths, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The region's economy rested on copper, on cattle and on a railway that carried both to the coast; its towns grew up around the mines, its politics were dominated by the mine owners and its schools were built with their money. Two things changed that: a strike in 1912 and the war that followed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial ' Two' enumerating new items added to the entity constructed over a long multi-clause history span, mirroring the claimed 'Two more' pattern, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The report argues that the agency ignored the warning signs for years, that senior staff suppressed the internal review and that the board signed off on the accounts without reading them. But I think the explanation is simpler: nobody was paying attention until the auditors arrived.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial contrastive ' But' plus anaphoric ' I' opening a second proposition that qualifies the report's claim built up over the preceding multi-clause span, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The trail climbs through pine forest for six miles, crosses a suspension bridge above a gorge and then follows the ridge for another four hours, with the summit hut visible the whole way but never getting closer. We reached it just before dark, tired, sunburned and out of water.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Measured sentence-initial anaphoric ' We' opening a second proposition that continues and qualifies the journey elaborated across the long preceding span, a travel-narrative genre, so the hypothesis predicts activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The samples were collected at four sites along the river, stored in amber glass, filtered within six hours and analyzed by two independent labs using different instruments, with the results compared blind to the site labels. However, they found no consistent difference between upstream and downstream concentrations.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial 'However' plus measured anaphoric ' they' opening a contrasting second proposition that qualifies the method-heavy claim built up over the span, so the hypothesis predicts activation.
